subject: Mid-quarter sync — prioritize latency SLOs & unblock infra experiments
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Amy Young <amy.young@amazon.com>, CloudBridge Ops <ops@cloudbridge.io>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-quarter sync — prioritize latency SLOs & unblock infra experiments

Team —

Quick mid-quarter status and a few concrete dependency asks ahead of QBR prep. High level: OKRs are mostly on track but two items are at risk if we don’t unblock infra decisions this week. I’m keeping this focused so we can escalate only what’s necessary.

Objective highlights (current status):
- O1: Reduce production P95 latency for streamed completions from ~120ms -> 80ms — at 65% progress. We’ve gotten model-level improvements but not infra. At risk.
- O2: Lower token cost by 12% via batching + KV prefix caching — 55% progress; needs canary rollout for a subset of routes.
- O3: Dedicated GA readiness — integration tests green, documentation incomplete but not blocking.

Top asks (need answers by Mon EOD PT):
1) NVMe allocation: infra approval to provision 10 additional NVMe-backed nodes in us-west-2 for latency experiments (will be used for L2 caching + kernel perf tests). File attached: infra_nvme_request.xlsx
2) Canary policy change: allow us to run continuous batching on route /v1/stream for 10% of prod traffic for 48 hours. Marcus, can you confirm rollback guardrails?
3) QBR slide deck: I attached a short proposal (qbr_latency_proposal_v2.pdf). Lauren — can you own final narrative and customer-facing metric?

Why this matters: if we can reduce tail latency to our target this quarter we unlock a higher SLA tier for Dedicated customers and materially reduce re-tries in real customer flows (CloudBridge shows 8% error increase when P95 > 100ms). Amy — sharing this with you so you have context for the marketplace ask.

Next steps: please reply with explicit yes/no for (1) and (2) and add any timing constraints. If we can’t get NVMe this week we should discuss re-scoping O1 to a 9-week plan instead of 6-week.

Thanks,
Karthik
VP, Platform Product
Redwood Inference

Attachment: qbr_latency_proposal_v2.pdf (10 pages)
Attachment: infra_nvme_request.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-quarter sync — prioritize latency SLOs & unblock infra experiments

Karthik —

Thanks for the concise ask. I dug into the draft deck and the customer metrics — two quick thoughts before I finalize narrative:

- Re-scope suggestion: given NVMe timing uncertainty, propose we split O1 into O1a (90-day tactical improvements we can guarantee w/o new infra) and O1b (experimental infra-backed gains). That keeps QBR messaging optimistic while being honest on risk.
- Customer-facing metric: propose we use user-impactible metric ("completed sessions with no retry") instead of raw P95. P95 is opaque to some execs.

I can own final slide deck if Marcus and Vivek confirm the canary plan and infra window. Tentative timeline: I’ll prepare a narrative draft by Tue noon PT.

-Lauren
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-quarter sync — prioritize latency SLOs & unblock infra experiments

Folks —

Quick infra reality check: additional NVMe nodes can be provisioned, but procurement and capacity reservations mean we can get them live in ~6 business days (not immediate). I attached a short SKU/timing table to the request spreadsheet. Operational risk: bringing NVMe for L2 cache will require a coordinated kernel rollout and we need a 4-hour maintenance window for the first deploy.

Regarding the canary: Marcus, please confirm that the runtime has a soft-rollback for continuous batching (we’ll throttle to 10% and monitor token cost + headroom). If we can commit to automatic rollback on 2% error delta or 25% cost overshoot, I can approve the canary window.

Also: we can offer a smaller interim win — spin up 4 NVMe instances (warm pool) in us-west-2 that we rotate into canary; this shortens lead time to ~3 business days with a larger on-cost. That would let us run an experiment before the heavier 10-node commit.

-Vivek
Head of Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Attachment: infra_nvme_request.xlsx (updated: timing + SKU notes)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-quarter sync — prioritize latency SLOs & unblock infra experiments

All —

Confirming canary gates: runtime supports soft rollback and we’ll instrument the following alarms before any traffic shift:
- 2%+ error rate delta across the canary routes
- 20% CPU/GPU utilization spike on canary nodes for >5 minutes
- Token cost delta > 18% vs baseline (we’ll log to cost stream)

I also support Vivek’s smaller warm-pool plan to accelerate experiments. If Karthik and Lauren are comfortable with a two-track messaging approach (O1a/O1b), I’ll schedule the canary for Wed morning PT after we provision the warm pool on Tue.

Next steps (agreed):
- Vivek: provision 4 NVMe warm-pool nodes by Tue EOD (if procurement clears).
- Marcus: readiness checklist + schedule canary Wed 08:00 PT.
- Lauren: narrative draft Tue 12:00 PT.
- Karthik: finalize QBR slide deck Tue 17:00 PT and circulate to Amy/CloudBridge for early feedback.

If any of these slip, we re-scope O1 timeline in the QBR narrative.

Thanks —
Marcus
Director, Runtime Engineering
Redwood Inference
